The [introduction](isoformic-introduction.html) uses GENCODE, but `prepare_isoformic_annotation()` does not depend on the GENCODE vocabulary.
Genes are features of a gene-like type or parents of transcripts, transcripts are features of a transcript-like type (`transcript`, `mRNA`, `lnc_RNA`, ...) or parents of exons, and identifiers are taken from `gene_id`/`transcript_id` attributes or from `ID`/`Parent`.
This article shows how to obtain and prepare the other references the downloader knows about.
Most chunks are not evaluated because they download gigabytes of data; every file lands in the package cache (`?isoformic-options`).

```{r}
#| message: false
library(isoformic)
```

## Telomere-to-telomere assembly (T2T-CHM13)

The same object works on the T2T-CHM13v2.0 assembly, with the NCBI RefSeq annotation or the Liftoff annotations of the T2T consortium:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# NCBI RefSeq annotation of T2T-CHM13v2.0: GFF3 + matching transcript FASTA
t2t_gff <- download_reference(reference = "t2t", file_type = "gff")
t2t_fasta <- download_reference(reference = "t2t", file_type = "fasta")
annot_t2t <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(t2t_gff)

# T2T consortium Liftoff annotations keep the GRCh38 identifiers of each
# lifted gene and transcript in `source_gene_id` / `source_transcript_id`
annot_lift <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(
  "chm13v2.0_GENCODEv35_CAT_Liftoff.vep.gff3.gz"
)
read_parquet(fs::path(annot_lift, "annot_data_transcripts.parquet"), n_max = 3)
```

For lifted annotations, build the transcript FASTA for Salmon from the assembly with `gffread -w transcripts.fa -g chm13v2.0.fa annotation.gff3`, and use `source_transcript_id` to join results obtained on GRCh38 (for example gene sets defined on GENCODE identifiers).
`extract_transcript_sequences(annot, genome_fasta = )` derives the transcript sequences from the assembly for the sequence-aware analyses.

## Ensembl, NCBI and MANE

The same downloader covers Ensembl (any division), any NCBI assembly accession and MANE, and arbitrary URLs:

```{r}
#| eval: false
ens_gff <- download_reference(reference = "ensembl")                       # current human release
ath_gff <- download_reference(reference = "ensembl", division = "plants",
                              species = "arabidopsis_thaliana")
grch38_refseq <- download_reference(reference = "ncbi", accession = "GCF_000001405.40")
mane_gff <- download_reference(reference = "mane")                         # canonical transcripts
```

Transcripts carry their `tags` (`MANE_Select`, `Ensembl_canonical`, `basic`, ...) and an `is_canonical` flag whatever the source, so `dominant_isoform()` and `transcript_features()` know the canonical isoform of each gene.

## Haplotype-resolved assemblies (trio binning, HPRC)

Phased assemblies come with one annotation per haplotype.
`merge_annotations()` combines them into one annotation directory whose identifiers carry a `_<haplotype>` suffix (rename the transcript FASTA headers the same way before indexing), and `haplotype_summary()` reports the expression of each gene per haplotype, the haplotype fraction and whether the dominant isoform differs between haplotypes:

```{r}
#| eval: false
files <- download_hprc_annotation("HG00438")           # HG00438.1.chm13.gff3.gz, HG00438.2.chm13.gff3.gz
merged <- merge_annotations(files, annot_name = "HG00438_chm13")
iso_hap <- read_salmon(quant_dirs, annot_path = merged)
haplotype_summary(iso_hap, group = "condition")
```

## FANTOM CAT and FANTOM6

The FANTOM CAT transcriptome assembly (the catalog used by FANTOM6) is read with its own variables: `geneClass` becomes the gene type and the type of transcripts without a biotype, and `geneCategory`, `DHS_type`, `coding_status`, `cumulative_support` and `TIEScore` are kept; the companion tables add the CAGE-defined promoter of every transcript (`cage_cluster_id`) and the gene information columns:

```{r}
#| eval: false
gtf <- download_reference(reference = "fantom", version = "lv3_robust", file_type = "gtf")
tables <- download_fantom_cat_tables("lv3_robust")
annot_fantom <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(gtf)
add_fantom_cat_tables(annot_fantom, tables[["id_mapping"]], tables[["gene_info"]])
```

## Long-read transcript catalogs

StringTie, Bambu, FLAIR or IsoQuant GTF files are read like any annotation; novel transcripts have no biotype until SQANTI3 structural categories are added, after which they behave as transcript types in every plot and summary:

```{r}
#| eval: false
annot_lr <- prepare_isoformic_annotation("flair_isoforms.gtf")
add_sqanti_classification(annot_lr, "flair_isoforms_classification.txt")
```

Novel transcripts have no annotated CDS, so the [sequence-aware ORFs](isoformic-productivity.html) derived from the genome are what classify them as productive or not.
